content.value_statement: Single-cell datasets require careful model choices and preprocessing before results are reliable. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through scvi-tools workflows for integration, differential expression, and multimodal analysis.
actual_capabilities: Explains scVI, scANVI, totalVI, MultiVI, PeakVI, DestVI, and other scvi-tools models by data modality.
Outlines AnnData setup, raw-count handling, covariate registration, model training, and result extraction workflows.
Guides batch correction, latent representation extraction, clustering, UMAP, and downstream Scanpy analysis.
Supports differential expression and differential accessibility setup with scvi-tools parameters and interpretation guidance.
Covers multimodal, spatial, methylation, cytometry, RNA velocity, doublet detection, and reference mapping workflows.
Summarizes hyperparameter tuning, GPU usage, memory management, and troubleshooting for large single-cell datasets.
limitations: Does not inspect private datasets unless the user provides data context or files.
Does not replace statistical review of biological conclusions or clinical validation.
May require scvi-tools, PyTorch, Scanpy, and GPU dependencies in the user environment.
Cannot guarantee model convergence or biological validity for low-quality input data.

use_cases.title: Plan an scRNA-seq Integration
use_cases.description: Choose scVI or scANVI, prepare AnnData fields, register covariates, and define downstream clustering steps.

use_cases.title: Select a Multimodal Model
use_cases.description: Compare totalVI, MultiVI, and MrVI for CITE-seq, multiome, paired, or unpaired data analysis.

use_cases.title: Troubleshoot Training at Scale
use_cases.description: Review hyperparameters, GPU settings, batch size, memory constraints, and convergence problems in scvi-tools workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Select a Model
prompt_templates.prompt: I have [data modality], [sample count], and [analysis goal]. Recommend the best scvi-tools model and explain the setup steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Analysis Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a scvi-tools workflow for [dataset type]. Include AnnData preparation, covariates, training, latent representation, and downstream analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Interpret Differential Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me interpret scvi-tools differential expression results for [groups]. Explain effect size, probability, FDR, and practical filtering choices.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Large-Scale Study
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a scalable scvi-tools plan for [large dataset]. Include model selection, GPU strategy, memory controls, validation checks, and saved artifacts.

output_examples.input: A user asks which model to use for paired RNA and ATAC data with missing modalities.
output: Recommends MultiVI because it supports paired and unpaired RNA plus ATAC observations.
Lists required modality labels in AnnData and notes that raw counts should be preserved.
Suggests checking joint latent space quality before interpreting imputed modalities.

output_examples.input: A user sees strong donor effects after training an scVI model.
output: Reviews whether donor, batch, and study labels were registered as covariates.
Suggests checking batch mixing against marker preservation in the latent space.
Identifies hyperparameters and quality-control issues that can weaken integration.

output_examples.input: A user wants differential expression between two T cell states.
output: Explains how to define groups, choose change mode, and set a practical effect-size threshold.
Describes how to interpret probability, Bayes factor, and false discovery values.
Warns against overinterpreting small groups without stability checks.

best_practices: Start from raw counts and preserve normalized data in separate layers.
Register meaningful batch, donor, and technical covariates before training models.
Save trained models and AnnData outputs for reproducible downstream analysis.
anti_patterns: Training scvi-tools models on log-normalized counts without a raw-count layer.
Interpreting latent clusters without checking batch mixing and biological markers.
Running differential expression without considering effect-size thresholds and group size imbalance.

faq.question: What data format does this skill expect?
faq.answer: It focuses on AnnData-based workflows, which are standard for scvi-tools and Scanpy analysis.

faq.question: Can it help install scvi-tools?
faq.answer: It can suggest installation commands, but the user controls all environment changes.

faq.question: Does it support CITE-seq data?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for totalVI and related multimodal workflows.

faq.question: Can it help with spatial transcriptomics?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers DestVI, Stereoscope, Tangram, and related spatial analysis patterns.

faq.question: Does it guarantee correct biological conclusions?
faq.answer: No. Results still need domain review, quality control, and appropriate validation.

faq.question: Is a GPU required?
faq.answer: No, but a GPU can greatly improve training speed for large datasets.
